title: Why use direct or indirect supply?

blocks.heading: Why use direct or indirect supply?
blocks.text: Direct selling can preserve contact with customers, control the offer and retain the share otherwise taken by intermediaries. The producer must then perform selling, storage, delivery and support or pay for them separately. Indirect channels can provide reach, local stock, specialist selling and smaller customer transactions, but intermediaries require a margin and can reduce producer control. Choose by target dispersion, volume, perishability, complexity and resources. Removing a retailer does not guarantee lower total cost if the producer takes on expensive fulfilment.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Kena Furniture makes customised items for a small number of nearby buyers. Another fictional producer supplies standard low-price items to many distant households. Direct contact may suit Kena’s detailed requirements. Retail intermediaries may suit dispersed standard sales if their reach is worth the margin. The decision depends on functions and costs, not a belief that intermediaries add no value.
